title: Canto Ostinato

wikipedia_after_all.detail: Article on the underlying work only; its Recordings section does not mention Erik Hall's 2023 version. No Wikipedia article for Erik Hall found.

facts: Played, recorded and mixed by Erik Hall at his home in Galien, Michigan, in October 2021
Three keyboards only: a 1962 Hammond M-101 organ, a 1978 Rhodes Mark I and his family's 1910 Steinway (Model O) grand
Each part played live and miked one at a time, no loops, quantizing or sequencing; page turns and noise left in
Second of a trilogy of minimalist reinterpretations after his 2020 Music for 18 Musicians (Reich)
Released 22 February 2023 on Western Vinyl; mastered by Warren Defever at Third Man Mastering, Detroit; art by Aaron Lowell Denton
Hall says the piece made him rebuild piano technique he had not kept up since his teens
Bandcamp Daily feature by Matthew Blackwell, 21 March 2023
Hall mapped his pacing after listening to several existing recordings of the 106 section score
Kept the length under an hour so it would fit a single LP
Read from the score while recording since he had not memorised it; chose a felted Steinway after trial and error
Hall is known from NOMO and In Tall Buildings; compares the home made feel to lo-fi indie rock
Third part of the trilogy not yet chosen at the time
PopMatters review by Chris Ingalls, 6 March 2023, 8/10
Notes the release came weeks after ten Holt's 100th birth anniversary (24 January 2023)
Repeats press facts: three keyboards, no loops or programming, five note motif running through 106 sections
A Closer Listen review, 12 February 2023
Describes the performer freedoms in the score (instruments, repeats, dynamics) and Hall's instrument choice
Hall is Chicago born and Michigan based, plays in NOMO and Wild Belle, records as In Tall Buildings
His Music for 18 Musicians won a Libera Award for best classical record; Canto Ostinato was nominated in the same category
Trilogy completed by Solo Three (Branca, Palestine, Spiegel, Reich)
Work completed 1976, first performed 1979 in Bergen, North Holland, on three pianos and an electric organ
106 short sections that performers may repeat at will; four pianos is the usual setup

Hall later performed both works with a spatial audio installation at National Sawdust (26 September 2026); a separate large ensemble Canto Ostinato with Metropolis Ensemble and Sandbox Percussion followed

example_line: Erik Hall recorded every part alone at his Michigan home in October 2021, on a 1910 Steinway, a Rhodes and a Hammond organ.
notes: Rich: label about text, a Bandcamp Daily interview and several reviews. Work article on Wikipedia gives background on the piece. Minor date spread (22 vs 24 February 2023) between sources.

title: Un peu de l'âme des bandits

wikipedia_after_all.detail: Full album article (about 1,000 words of prose) plus a Dutch version. Matcher likely missed it on the Aqsak/Aksak spelling and title capitalisation.

facts: Recorded February and August 1979 at Sunrise Studio, Kirchberg, Switzerland; released January 1980 on Marc Hollander's Crammed Discs
Sleeve spells the band Aqsak Maboul; the 1995 CD reissue went back to Aksak
Guests include ex Henry Cow members Fred Frith and Chris Cutler and Michel Berckmans of Univers Zero; Vincent Kenis arranged two tracks without playing
Side B is the 23 minute Cinema suite ending in a mock Bulgarian radio talk show; Tango was built from cut up tango records
Tied to the Rock in Opposition movement; AllMusic 4.5 stars, Pitchfork 7.2 for the 2018 reissue
Second album, first released January 1980
Placed third in NME's 1980 list of top European albums
2018 vinyl reissue remastered from the analogue tapes, with a 24 page booklet and liner notes by Mikey IQ Jones
Bonus CD Before and After Bandits: ten unreleased live and demo tracks from 1977 to 1980
Sessions began February 1979; unfinished after a month, the band returned in August to finish
Core quartet Hollander, Kenis, Frank Wuyts and Marc Moulin, with Catherine Jauniaux, Denis Van Hecke and Berckmans as guests
First Aksak Maboul release on Crammed; debut had flopped on the small Kamikaze label
I Viaggi is a traditional Turkish tune; pinball flipper sounds and taped sounds used before samplers
Quietus review of the reissue; frames it as the first Crammed Discs release
Uncut, March 2018: reviews the reissue, rates the extras 8/10 and describes the Before and After Bandits bonus

example_line: Recorded at Sunrise Studio in Kirchberg, Switzerland, in 1979, with Fred Frith and Chris Cutler of Henry Cow as guests.
notes: A Wikipedia album article exists after all. Plenty for notes even without it (label about text, reissue booklet, blog history).

title: Perpetuum Mobile

wikipedia_after_all.detail: Only a one sentence mention of the band Mariani in Eric Johnson's Early life section; the album is not named. en Perpetuum_Mobile_(album) is the Einsturzende Neubauten record.

facts: Sonobeat (Austin) recorded the power trio around drummer Vince Mariani in March and April 1970
Neighbours complained about the Marshall amps at the home studio, so basic tracks for Perpetuum Mobile moved to a vacant 100 acre ranch near McDade, east of Austin
Vocal overdubs and jazz intercuts were added at the Western Hills Drive studio; first sessions on Sonobeat's new 16 input console
Single Re-Birth Day / Memories Lost and Found issued 8 September 1970 (Sonobeat R-s118)
Lineup Vince Mariani (drums), Eric Johnson (guitar), Jay Podolnick (bass, vocals), who wrote the songs together
Vince Mariani nearly auditioned for Hendrix's band before producer Bill Josey persuaded him to form his own group
Johnson was about 15 or 16; band toured with acts such as Deep Purple, then split without a second record
Quotes Johnson's FAQ: about 100 copies pressed to court a major label, no deal came, band broke up in spring 1970
Johnson neither sang nor wrote on it per that FAQ; many later bootleg CDs miscredit it
Lists plain white sleeves stamped Advance Copy; tracklist and a 2001 re-release
Johnson joined Mariani, a psychedelic rock act, at about 15; start of his professional career

example_line: Its basic tracks were recorded on an empty ranch near McDade, Texas, with Eric Johnson, then about 15, on guitar.
notes: Sources conflict on date (Johnson's FAQ says a fall 1969 demo; Sonobeat says March/April 1970) and on vocals (Podolnick vs Bill Wilson). The producer is Bill Josey (Sonobeat), misspelled Posey in one review. Notes are possible but should hedge the dates.

title: Le sacre du printemps

wikipedia_after_all.detail: Large article on the work (The Rite of Spring) mentions only that Stravinsky re-recorded it in 1940; the discography list has one table row (Columbia/CBS, 4 x 78 rpm, Sony CD 2013).

facts: Row: New York Philharmonic, Stravinsky conducting, Columbia/CBS, four 78 rpm discs, Sony CD 2013
Stravinsky recorded the work after 1929 again in 1940 and 1960; full history of the 1913 ballet
Sedgwick Clark, Musical America, 6 June 2013, survey of 49 recordings
Session date 29 April 1940 (the Sony package wrongly prints 4 April)
Reissued as CD 2 of Sony's 100th anniversary Sacre set, about 31 minutes
Calls it tight, a clear advance on Stravinsky's 1929 Paris recording, with some stumbles in the closing Danse sacrale
Audiophile Audition review of Naxos Historical 8.112070, pairing the 1940 Rite with 1940/1946 Firebird and Petrushka, restored by Mark Obert-Thorn
Richard Ginell survey: the 1940 version is pushed harder, with more tempo changes in Part II; available on Sony and Pearl

example_line: Stravinsky himself conducted the New York Philharmonic for this 1940 Columbia recording, first issued on four 78 rpm discs.
notes: Notes would lean on the work's history (well covered) plus a few recording facts. Session venue unconfirmed (one database says Carnegie Hall; Liederkranz Hall is for Petrushka). Which reissue the Spotify album is was not checked.

title: Surreal Overdose

wikipedia_after_all.detail: Band article names the album in History and Discography (2011, Shrieks From the Hearse with PATAC Records); no album article.

facts: Label news, 16 May 2011: first full length of new material since As the Weird Travels On (2005)
Released by PATAC Records with the band's own Shrieks From the Hearse; vinyl by Hell's Headbangers
Recorded at Assembly Line Studios, Virginia, engineered by Kevin Gutierrez, produced by King Fowley
Fowley back on drums and vocals; Shane Fuegel replaced Mark Adams (retired 2007); Mike Smith studio guitar; Les Snyder bass
Sean Palmerston, July 2011: Fowley's first studio drumming since Supernatural Addiction (2000)
Songs as self contained horror and B movie science fiction stories
Fowley sold the reviewer a copy at Maryland Deathfest and called it the band's most explosive
8.5/10; eight songs including the seven minute Skin Crawling Progress; vocoded vocals on Cloned (Day of the Robot)
User review, 4/5; little changed since the previous album
Short Last Rites write up: familiar elements done well
2016 reissue on Lost Apparitions Records (Luray, Virginia), catalogue 030; no album about text
Album named with year and labels only

example_line: King Fowley went back to the drums here; it was recorded at Assembly Line Studios in Virginia, with Fowley producing.
notes: Encyclopaedia Metallum returned 403 to WebFetch, so its entry was not read. Notes of 150 words are reachable from the label news plus reviews, but thin on the idea behind the record.

artist: György Ligeti & Berliner Philharmoniker & Jonathan Nott
title: The Ligeti Project II: Lontano; Atmosphères; Apparitions; San Francisco Polyphony; Concert românesc

wikipedia_after_all.detail: The Atmospheres article's Discography section names this recording (Philharmonie, 13 to 16 December 2001; Teldec 2002; 2008 box). Works Lontano, San Francisco Polyphony etc. have their own articles; no article for the Ligeti Project series or this disc.

facts: Tony Haywood, MusicWeb International, February 2003; Teldec 8573-88261-2
Recorded at the Philharmonie, Berlin, 13 to 16 December 2001; two performances live
First recordings of Concert romanesc (1951) and of Apparitions, which premiered in Cologne in 1960
Liner notes by Ligeti himself; compares Nott's Lontano and Atmospheres with Abbado's 1994 Vienna disc
Lists this recording, released 2002 on Teldec/Warner as The Ligeti Project II, reissued 2008 as disc 2 of a five CD set
Classics Today review: praises the sound and Ligeti's notes; Teldec filling a gap left by Sony's Ligeti Edition
Sacramento News & Review: Lontano and Atmospheres, the latter known from Kubrick's 2001
Warner Classics: series close to Ligeti's heart, composer involved in the recordings until his death in 2006
Publisher: Concert romanesc a camouflage piece of 1951, banned after one rehearsal in Budapest, not performed until 1971

example_line: The Berlin Philharmonic and Jonathan Nott recorded it at the Berlin Philharmonie in December 2001, with notes by Ligeti himself.
notes: Plenty: the works themselves are well documented, plus disc specific review facts (dates, premiere recordings, Ligeti's own notes).

title: ザ・ノイズ (The Noise)

wikipedia_after_all.detail: One row in the discography's box set table (2009, 30 CDs) and a citation of Jojo Hiroshige's 2009 liner notes in the Hijokaidan article; no prose about it. No ja.wikipedia album article found.

facts: Read through api.discogs.com/releases/1830052 (the HTML page returns 403)
Full title The Noise - 30th Anniversary - 1979-2009; Alchemy Records ARCD-187 to 216; released 16 June 2009, Japan
30 CD box, limited to 500 hand numbered copies, with a 32 page booklet of Japanese and English notes, photos, discography and live dates
Mostly unreleased material; exceptions are the 1982 album on CD5, two discs of the 1992 box on CD17/18 and a 2002 LP side
Produced and annotated by Jojo Hiroshige; remastered by Ippei Suda at LM Studio in 2009; murky sound is intentional per the notes
Spans Kyoto recordings from October 1979 to a studio session at Meidaimae Studio, Tokyo, 25 April 2009, incl. a 2005 Scotland show and a John Duncan session
Disc by disc review, 19 September 2009
CD1 to 3 by the original lineup; a Janis Joplin cover on CD23; solo tracks by Mikawa, Jojo, Kosakai and Junko on CD28; side projects such as Acid Mothers Kaidan on CD29
Booklet with a band history written by Jojo Hiroshige
August 2009 post tracing phases in the box: prog inspired jams, confrontational performances, band noise rock, later walls of noise
Listed under box sets, 2009, 30 CDs; liner notes titled The Thirtieth Anniversary of Hijokaidan dated 19 June 2009

example_line: A box of 30 CDs, limited to 500 numbered copies, tracing Hijokaidan from their Kyoto start in 1979 to a 2009 Tokyo session.
notes: Important: this is a 30 CD anniversary box set, not a single album; RYM files it as an album. Standard search missed it (also in Japanese); an extended search found Discogs and the blogs. Discogs public API worked when discogs.com pages gave 403. suruga-ya.jp also 403.

facts: Ensemble's own page: ten women's voices directed by Barbara Thornton, with fiddler Elizabeth Gaver
Only Sequentia recording without Benjamin Bagby

Part of Sequentia's complete Hildegard project with WDR; programme built around St. Ursula and her 11,000 virgin companions martyred at Cologne
57 page booklet available as PDF (not read)

On this disc she sings the invocation in Hildegard's sequence for St. Ursula

title: Midtown 120 Blues

facts: First full length as DJ Sprinkles; Mule Musiq, 9 August 2008, 79:46; reissued 2014 on Thaemlitz's Comatonse
Opens with a spoken intro tying deep house to the AIDS crisis, ACT UP, police violence and racism
Ball'r (Madonna-Free Zone) ends with a speech on Vogue erasing ballroom culture's Black, Latino and queer roots
Resident Advisor album of the year 2009; Pitchfork Best New Reissue 8.5 (2014)
Excerpt of Luis-Manuel Garcia's Resident Advisor feature, 28 January 2014, hosted by Comatonse
Title refers to Midtown's 42nd Street red light strip, the 120 bpm of 1990s New York deep house, and the blues
Thaemlitz DJed in the early 1990s at Sally's II, a club for trans sex workers, and lost the residency in 1992 for refusing major label records
2014 deluxe CD reissue on Comatonse with a large poster, out 31 May
No vinyl because the album's phase based bass placement would cancel when cut in mono
Resident Advisor review, 4.5/5

example_line: The title names the Midtown strip where Terre Thaemlitz DJed at Sally's II, and the 120 bpm of 1990s New York deep house.
